minutes.headline: Select Board moved to deny a one-day entertainment license for 300 Holman Street after neighbor opposition.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was a contested hearing on a one-day entertainment license for a Holman Street property. Town counsel explained the board's authority, and many abutters objected. A motion to deny was made and seconded; the count was not captured. The board also approved licenses, ratified an assistant town clerk, heard the town manager's report, approved an economic development survey and a letter opposing House bill 4075, and went into executive session.

what_happened.line: A motion to deny a one-day entertainment license for 300 Holman Street as a nuisance was made after a long hearing; the count was not audible.
Neighbors spoke against the license on parking, noise, septic and safety grounds, while the host said donations were optional and the event was not a business.
The board took up common victualler licenses, a 90-day closure for the Bootlegger and a ratification of an assistant town clerk; counts were not audible.
A motion to send a letter opposing House bill 4075, with a minor change, was made; the count was not audible.
The board agreed to take the tax-increase concern up at the budget meeting, then went into executive session.

why_it_matters: The Holman Street hearing shows how the board applies its licensing authority to private events that draw neighbors' complaints, which bears on events in residential areas.
The tax-increase concern was deferred to the budget meeting, so any effect on a tax bill will be discussed there rather than decided here.
watch_next: The budget meeting, where the board agreed to take up the tax-increase concern.
Next week's meeting, which is to include the to-do list and the engineers' property assessment presentation.
